issue.author: internal-review-repo
issue.body:
**What is needed:** the k-grid sensitivity run behind the paper's sentence "A grid k in {1,...,30} gave the same conclusion (code/README.md)", delivered as code and results.

**What it is for:** R16 ("the code that produced every number"). It is also your own commitment that "one command reproduces every number". The numbers in `report/code/README.md` (kNN 94.40, difference +1.00 pp with corrected CI [-2.39, +4.39], naive CI [+0.08, +1.92]) come from your commit 6950192. Its results are not in the delivery, and the delivered `cv.py` cannot produce them because `K_GRID` is hard-coded to odd k.

**What I already know:** the claim is true. In a pinned venv (numpy 2.1.3, scipy 1.14.1, sklearn 1.5.2) I changed `K_GRID` to `list(range(1, 31))` and re-ran. All four numbers came out exactly as in the README. Everything else in your part is verified end to end: the from-scratch re-run is byte-identical, analyze.py outputs are byte-identical, and Ibex job 53909243 is confirmed on cn504-26 via sacct. Details are in `review/record.md` of internal-review-repo (commit d9c907e6b1e44aba281ab3a925ced4239ac9390e).

**What would close it:**
- a delivered way to run the 1..30 grid from `report/code/`, e.g. an optional grid argument to `cv.py` with the default unchanged, or a small separate script;
- its per-fold results and the summary numbers quoted in the README under `report/results/` (e.g. `results/sensitivity_k1-30/`), generated by delivered code;
- `code/README.md` pointing to those files and giving the command.

Keep the main local and Ibex outputs byte-identical. Do not change what `cv.py` writes for the main grid. No action is needed on the `np.float64(...)` repr in the `inner_acc_knn` column (see the record's non-blocking notes).

**What waits on it:** my approval of the delivery.

issue.body:
**What I need** (for `report/report.pdf`, the two-page NeurIPS 2026 paper the objective asks for), delivered in experiment-repo under these paths so the assembled delivery puts them next to the PDF (I will ask story-repo to put these paths in the assignment):

1. `report/code/` — the code that produced every number: OpenML download of dataset 61, the 10×stratified 5-fold CV comparing multinomial LR vs kNN (k chosen by inner CV), interval computation, the Ibex SLURM job script, the local run, and the local-vs-Ibex comparison. Pinned versions (lock file / requirements) and seeds.
2. `report/results/` — raw per-fold accuracies (both runs), a summary file, the Ibex job log showing the node name (e.g. `$SLURMD_NODENAME`), and the identical/not-identical verdict with how it was checked (bitwise on per-fold accuracies?).
3. **`report/results/numbers.tex`** — LaTeX macros generated by your code, so I never hand-type a number. Please use these names (values as you would print them, e.g. `0.973`):
   - `\LRmean`, `\LRlo`, `\LRhi` ; `\KNNmean`, `\KNNlo`, `\KNNhi` ; `\DIFFmean`, `\DIFFlo`, `\DIFFhi` (LR − kNN)
   - `\Nsamples`, `\Nreps`, `\Nfolds`, `\Kgrid` (the k candidates as text), `\Kmode` (most frequently selected k), `\IbexNode`, `\RunsIdentical` (`yes`/`no`), `\IntervalMethod` (one short phrase, e.g. "corrected resampled t (Nadeau–Bengio)")
   - anything else you think the text needs; tell me the names.
4. `report/figures/<name>.pdf` — the one figure (vector PDF, single column width ≈ 5.5 in, readable at that size), plus a one-sentence statement of the claim it supports.
5. `report/tables/<name>.tex` — the one table as a `booktabs` `tabular` body (I wrap it in `table` with caption), e.g. rows LR / kNN / difference, columns mean, 95% interval.

**What it is for**: the paper's results section, its table and figure, and the reproducibility statement (Ibex node, identical runs).

**What I know**: Iris has 150 samples, 3 balanced classes; naive t intervals over 50 correlated folds are too narrow, so please state which interval you use and why (I will cite it, e.g. Nadeau & Bengio 2003, and need the reference if different).

**What waits**: the results paragraphs, table, figure and README map in the report. I am drafting the template, structure and methods text now against these macro names.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Delivered at `7db61f9` (experiment-repo `main`); all five items.

1. **Code** `report/code/` — `fetch_data.py` (OpenML 61, md5 checked), `cv.py` (full nested CV; seeds, threads pinned to 1), `ibex_job.sbatch`, `analyze.py` (intervals, local-vs-Ibex comparison, figure, table, macros), `requirements.txt`, `README.md` (commands, design, interval reference).
2. **Results** `report/results/` — `local/` and `ibex/` each with `folds.csv` (correct out of 30, accuracy, chosen k per outer fold), `predictions.csv` (all 1500 test predictions), `run_info.json` (host, CPU, versions, threads); `ibex/ibex_53909243.log` (first line: `node: cn504-26 job: 53909243`); `summary.json` → `reproducibility`. **Identity check:** byte-for-byte comparison (sha256) of both `folds.csv` and `predictions.csv` → identical, chosen k identical, max |Δacc| = 0. Note: local run was an Intel Xeon Gold 6230, Ibex an AMD EPYC 9655, same pinned numpy 2.1.3 / scipy 1.14.1 / scikit-learn 1.5.2.
3. **Macros** `report/results/numbers.tex` — accuracies in **percent, 2 decimals** (`\LRmean`=95.40 etc.); `\DIFF*` are signed percentage points and already contain `$+$`/`$-$` (use in text mode). All your names, plus: `\LRloNaive \LRhiNaive \KNNloNaive \KNNhiNaive \DIFFloNaive \DIFFhiNaive` (naive t, contrast), `\DIFFp` (corrected-t two-sided p for difference), `\FoldsLRbetter \FoldsTied \FoldsKNNbetter` (13/32/5), `\Nouter`(50) `\Ninner`(5) `\Ntrain`(120) `\Ntest`(30), `\Kmin \Kmax \Kmedian`, `\Seed`, `\DataMD` (md5), `\LRconvWarnings`(0), `\IbexJob \IbexCPU \IbexSeconds \LocalCPU \LocalSeconds`, `\PyVersion \SklearnVersion \NumpyVersion \ScipyVersion`. `\Kgrid` is math `$\{1, 3, \dots, 31\}$`. Compiled with booktabs in a test doc: no errors.
4. **Figure** `report/figures/fig_accuracy.pdf` (5.5 × 2.05 in, vector). Claim: *LR's mean accuracy is about one point higher than k-NN's, but the paired difference is within fold-to-fold noise: the corrected 95% interval for LR − k-NN spans 0, while the naive interval, which treats the 50 overlapping folds as independent, would wrongly exclude 0.* Suggested caption: "(a) Mean accuracy of each of the 10 CV repetitions (dots, joined by repetition) with the overall mean and corrected-t 95% CI. (b) Paired LR − k-NN accuracy difference on each of the 50 outer folds (30 test cases each, so differences come in steps of 3.33 pp; 32 folds tie), with the mean and the corrected-t (primary) and naive-t 95% CIs."
5. **Table** `report/tables/tab_results.tex` — booktabs `tabular` body: rows LR / k-NN / difference; columns mean, corrected-t 95% CI, naive-t 95% CI.

**Interval** (cite): Nadeau & Bengio (2003), "Inference for the Generalization Error", *Machine Learning* 52(3):239–281; corrected repeated-CV t as in Bouckaert & Frank (2004), "Evaluating the Replicability of Significance Tests for Comparing Learning Algorithms", PAKDD 2004, LNCS 3056:3–12. var = (1/J + n_test/n_train)s², J=50, t with 49 df.

**What it means for the text:** results support "no detectable difference" (p = `\DIFFp`), not "LR is better". Robustness: an earlier run with k ∈ {1..30} gave the same conclusion (numbers in `report/code/README.md`).

Follow-up at `e27d36f98a0d1806bd62414db44ed44426f2d1a7`: renamed to the names your draft reads — `report/figures/accuracy.pdf`, `report/tables/results.tex` (old `fig_accuracy.pdf`/`tab_results.tex` removed) — and added every macro your `report.tex` uses: `\Nevals` `\NtestFold` `\KNNinnerFolds` `\Seeds` `\IdenticalCheck` `\LRdetails` `\KNNdetails` `\DataChecksum` `\IbexJobId` `\PythonVersion` (differs: 3.11.2 local, 3.11.0 Ibex; numpy/scipy/scikit-learn identical) `\SklearnVersion`.

I built your `report/` at 3168d62 with my four directories overlaid: latexmk succeeds, 2 pages, no undefined macros. Three things in the text the results need:
1. **Units:** `\LRmean` etc. are percent and `\DIFF*` are percentage points, without the unit; the text currently prints "95.40 (95% interval 91.56–99.24)" — add \% / "pp".
2. **Figure caption:** left panel is not per-fold accuracies; it is the **mean accuracy of each of the 10 repetitions** (joined by repetition) with the overall mean and corrected-t 95% CI as a vertical bar per method. Right panel: the 50 per-fold differences as stacked dots (steps of 3.33 pp, 32 ties), with mean and **both** corrected-t (primary) and naive-t 95% CIs. Suggested caption is in my previous comment.
3. **Claim:** the corrected interval for the difference covers 0 (`\DIFFp` = 0.54); the text should say no detectable difference, and that the naive interval (table) would exclude 0 only because it ignores the overlap between training sets.

**What is needed:** two small corrections to `report/report.tex`, then a rebuilt `report/report.pdf`. The PDF must stay within two pages.

- **P1, precision of the reproducibility claim.** "The two runs are identical on two different CPU architectures" overstates the claim. Both CPUs are x86-64: Intel Xeon Gold 6230 locally and AMD EPYC 9655 on Ibex. They differ in vendor and microarchitecture, not in instruction-set architecture. Suggested wording: "on two different CPUs (Intel Xeon Gold 6230 and AMD EPYC 9655, both x86-64)", or "two different CPU models/microarchitectures".
- **P2, software citation.** Every result comes from scikit-learn implementations: LogisticRegression/lbfgs, KNeighborsClassifier, GridSearchCV and RepeatedStratifiedKFold. The paper names the version but does not cite scikit-learn. The brief (section 4) lists Pedregosa et al. (2011), "Scikit-learn: Machine learning in Python", JMLR 12:2825-2830, as the conventional citation. Add it to `references.bib` and cite it where the methods or versions are stated. Page 2 has room for one more reference.

**What it is for:** R13 and R16. These are claims stated no further than the evidence supports, and the conventions of the field for the paper.

**What I already know:** everything else in the paper is verified. I rendered and read both pages. Recompiling with TeX Live 2026 gives identical text, with no warnings or unresolved references. The style file matches the official NeurIPS 2026 zip, and submission mode is set. All numbers match my independent recomputation and the results files. There is exactly one figure and one table. Details are in `review/record.md` of internal-review-repo (commit d9c907e6b1e44aba281ab3a925ced4239ac9390e).

There is also a separate finding (E1) for experiment-repo. Its sensitivity results for the k in 1..30 grid will be delivered under `report/results/`, and `code/README.md` will point to them. Your sentence "(code/README.md)" can stay as is, unless you prefer to cite the results path once it exists.

**What waits on it:** my approval of the delivery.
